\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{منصرف} \fa{شدن} (monsaref shodan)}{منصرف شدن (monsaref shodan)}]{\fa{منصرف} \fa{شدن} (monsaref shodan) — to change one's mind, to give up an idea}

\label{lesson:FA-C396-monsaref-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for as soon as, then the Persian for as long as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{منصرف} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{منصرف} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{monsaref shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to change one's mind, to give up an idea\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{از} \fa{سفر} \fa{منصرف} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u az safar monsaref shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He decided not to go on the trip.
\end{quote}

It takes \emph{az}: \emph{az chizi monsaref shodan}. Stem \emph{shav-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{منصرف}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{munṣarif} \textquotedblleft{}turning away\textquotedblright{}; with the Persian verb \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}, you turn away from a plan.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{monsaref shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{monsaref shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{monsaref shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for as soon as, then the Persian for as long as, then say \emph{monsaref shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عقب} \fa{انداختن} ('aqab andâkhtan)}{عقب انداختن ('aqab andâkhtan)}]{\fa{عقب} \fa{انداختن} ('aqab andâkhtan) — to put off, to delay}

\label{lesson:FA-C396-aqab-andakhtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for as long as, then the Persian for to change one's mind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عقب} \fa{انداختن}}
\textbf{\fa{عقب} \fa{انداختن}} (\emph{'aqab andâkhtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to put off, to delay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جلسه} \fa{را} \fa{یک} \fa{هفته} \fa{عقب} \fa{انداختند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jalase râ yek hafte 'aqab andâkhtand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They put the meeting off by a week.
\end{quote}

\emph{'aqab} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} + \emph{andâkhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{andâz-}): to throw something back.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{عقب} \fa{انداختن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to throw back\textquotedblright{}: \emph{'aqab} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{'aqab}, and \emph{andâkhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{} is a native Persian verb listed in EtymDB.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'aqab andâkhtan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'aqab andâkhtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'aqab andâkhtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for as long as, then the Persian for to change one's mind, then say \emph{'aqab andâkhtan} again
\end{itemize}

\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداختن} (be ta'viq andâkhtan)}{به تعویق انداختن (be ta'viq andâkhtan)}]{\fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداختن} (be ta'viq andâkhtan) — to postpone}

\label{lesson:FA-C396-be-taviq-andakhtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to change one's mind, then the Persian for to put off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداختن}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداختن}} (\emph{be ta'viq andâkhtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to postpone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دانشگاه} \fa{امتحانها} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dâneshgâh emtehânhâ râ be ta'viq andâkht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The university postponed the exams.
\end{quote}

Formal. Without an object: \emph{be ta'viq oftâdan} — to be postponed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{تعویق} \fa{انداختن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to throw into delay\textquotedblright{}: \emph{ta'viq} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ta'wīq} \textquotedblleft{}delaying\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{andâkhtan} \textquotedblleft{}to throw\textquotedblright{} is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردن} (hamâhang kardan)}{هماهنگ کردن (hamâhang kardan)}]{\fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردن} (hamâhang kardan) — to coordinate, to arrange}

\label{lesson:FA-C396-hamahang-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to put off, then the Persian for to postpone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{hamâhang kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to coordinate, to arrange\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{من} \fa{با} \fa{همکارانم} \fa{زمان} \fa{جلسه} \fa{را} \fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{man bâ hamkârânam zamân-e jalase râ hamâhang kardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I arranged the meeting time with my colleagues.
\end{quote}

\emph{Hamâhang} \textquotedblleft{}in harmony\textquotedblright{}: \emph{ham} \textquotedblleft{}same\textquotedblright{} + \emph{âhang} \textquotedblleft{}tune\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Bâ kasi hamâhang kardan} — to arrange something with someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{هماهنگ} \fa{کردن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{ham} \textquotedblleft{}same, together\textquotedblright{} + \emph{âhang} \textquotedblleft{}tune\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian \emph{āhang}, + \emph{kardan}. To coordinate is to put people in one tune.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to put off, then the Persian for to postpone, then say \emph{hamâhang kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اجرا} \fa{کردن} (ejrâ kardan)}{اجرا کردن (ejrâ kardan)}]{\fa{اجرا} \fa{کردن} (ejrâ kardan) — to carry out, to perform}

\label{lesson:FA-C396-ejra-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to postpone, then the Persian for to coordinate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اجرا} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اجرا} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ejrâ kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to carry out, to perform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شهرداری} \fa{طرح} \fa{تازه} \fa{را} \fa{اجرا} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahrdâri tarh-e tâze râ ejrâ kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The town council carried out the new plan.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ejrâ} \textquotedblleft{}carrying out\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. Also to perform music or a play.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اجرا}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ijrā'} \textquotedblleft{}making something run, putting it into effect\textquotedblright{}; Persian drops the final hamza and adds \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
